title: Enforce the operational stored contract without historical reinterpretation
statement: The Work records Module shall enforce the associated v4 SQLite store and supported schema on every ordinary entry path, with no legacy execution fallback or historical reinterpretation.

what.problem: An operational reader or recovery path can silently restore withdrawn stored-format support even when command admission rejects it.
what.desired_outcome: Every persistence entry path enforces the same current stored boundary while historical content retains its original meaning.

why.rationale: SR-040 requires stored-contract rejection behind public dispatch; MOD-011 owns the records and recovery state that must enforce it.

stakeholders: Engineers and agents supplying explicit command requests
Maintainers of MOD-011 and its Interface consumers

conditions: An ordinary task or query opens the associated project store, or explicit maintenance validates a replacement/import candidate.

contexts: The IF-003 operational-record boundary and the selected store, candidates, and recovery material it governs.

how.approach: Check project association and database schema before current interpretation. Keep command, stored-record, database and backup versions independent; imports use only qualified source adapters.

how_much.scope: Current v4 ordinary operation and explicit supported maintenance. Historical v3 originals are read only by the qualified source importer or repository historical validator, never an ordinary runtime fallback.

acceptance_criteria: New current records identify rigorloop-records-v4 and schema_version 4 in the associated project database; PRAGMA schema version and project metadata are separately validated.
Unknown or mismatched projects, unsupported database schemas and corrupt stores stop safely without initializing an empty substitute.
Legacy directory or journal residue cannot select an executable backend or trigger recovery; original records remain unchanged by ordinary access.
Qualified explicit import preserves selected source originals and dispositions; it does not promote earlier judgments or bypass ordinary current-record validation.

sources.basis: Derive this draft lower-level obligation from the containing SR at the selected command or operational-record responsibility boundary. Allocation and acceptance criteria are design claims for review, not implementation, requirement approval, or satisfaction evidence.

sources.locator: docs/design/cli/cli.md#CLI-SR-10, CLI-SR-27, CLI-SR-28; docs/design/cli/records.md#RF-SR-01, RF-SR-06, RF-SR-09, RF-SR-12, RF-SR-14
sources.basis: Preserve the applicable current public and stored-record guarantees at this accountable boundary. The named source retains exact schemas, operation tables, classifications, limits, and historical adoption obligations; this allocation neither replaces those details nor accepts REM authoring JSON as operational records.

Reconcile the complete existing allocation with the selected current v2/v4 contract, preserving independent admission, coherent state, explicit scope and actor judgment. Prior version-specific sources retain their historical meaning.
